key_insight: A wall-resolved iLES database can reproduce bypass transition in flat-plate boundary layers with high fidelity and exposes major weaknesses in standard RANS transition models.
engineering_relevance: This database provides a realistic benchmark for improving transition prediction in aerodynamic and turbomachinery design, especially for data-driven and physics-informed closures.
method: High-order compressible Navier-Stokes solver with wall-resolved implicit LES
Multiple freestream turbulence levels and both zero and varying pressure gradients
Configured to closely mimic ERCOFTAC T3 flat-plate experiments
evidence_signal: The simulations show satisfactory agreement with legacy experiments for skin friction, mean velocity, and fluctuation profiles, while SA-BCM and k-ω-γ models systematically mispredict transition onset and length.
watch_item: The database is high-fidelity but still tied to specific flat-plate, bypass-transition conditions, so transfer to other geometries or transition mechanisms should be validated carefully.
paper_title: A high-fidelity numerical database for free-stream transition
